Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.server

Class EyeItemService

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.server.EyeItemService

Loader-neutral implementation of applying and harvesting googly-eye items.

  • Method Details

    • interact

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult interact(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob)
      Right-click-on-entity entry point for both eye items. A Slimy Eye returns InteractionResult.SUCCESS on the client and defers the mutation to the server; an Optometrist-shears harvest runs server-side only, dropping one eye and clearing the mob's eyes before returning SUCCESS. Every other case â€” plain shears, no Optometrist, an eyeless mob, a mob with no config, googlyEyesEnabled off, or the client side of the shears path â€” returns InteractionResult.PASS so the vanilla interaction is left to proceed.

    • useOnSkull

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult useOnSkull(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult hit)
      Right-click-on-block entry point for both eye items aimed at a placed mob head: a Slimy Eye goes to applySlimyEye(ItemStack, ServerPlayer, SkullBlockEntity, Direction), Optometrist shears on an eyed head to harvestSkull(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand, net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.SkullBlockEntity, net.minecraft.core.Direction). The client answers InteractionResult.SUCCESS in exactly those cases, so it neither runs nor sends the item's own use on top (a sneaking player's self-apply or self-shear). Anything else, including plain shears, returns InteractionResult.PASS.

    • applySlimyEye

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult applySlimyEye(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity target)
      The Slimy Eye apply verb, server side: an eyeless target passing the shared eligibility predicate gains eyes carrying the stack's appearance on a freshly rolled placement variant, consuming one eye. An already-eyed or ineligible target refuses (FAIL) and consumes nothing, as does any target while googlyEyesEnabled is off â€” the master switch blocks hand application the same as it blocks the at-spawn roll. Applying to another player additionally requires server PvP to be enabled and canHarmPlayer to hold, so it can't be used to restyle a teammate or anyone in a PvP-off world. Both the mob path (interact(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand, net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity)) and the sneak self-apply (SlimyEyeItem#use) route through here.

    • applySlimyEye

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult applySlimyEye(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.SkullBlockEntity skull, net.minecraft.core.Direction face)
      The Slimy Eye apply verb for a placed mob head, server side, clicked on its face: an eyeless head whose mob has an adult definition gains eyes carrying the stack's appearance on a freshly rolled placement variant, consuming one eye outside creative. The player must be allowed to use the item on that block, as placing a block there would require. Otherwise, or while googlyEyesEnabled is off, it refuses (FAIL) and consumes nothing.

    • harvestSkull

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult harvestSkull(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.SkullBlockEntity skull, net.minecraft.core.Direction face)
      The Optometrist harvest for a placed mob head, server side, clicked on its face: one Googly Eye carrying the head's effective appearance pops out of the block, the head loses its eyes, the shears in hand lose one durability, the shearing sound plays, and GameEvent.SHEAR is emitted. The player must be allowed to use the shears on that block. Returns InteractionResult.PASS when it doesn't apply (no eyes, not allowed, googlyEyesEnabled off).

    • markHeadDrop

      public static void markHeadDrop(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Give a head item an eyed mob drops in its death loot the mob's whole eye state, when the head is the mob's own kind (SkullEyeState.entityFor(net.minecraft.world.level.block.Block)) and carries no eyes yet, so the placed head shows the mob's arrangement and colors. Players are left out: their death drops are their inventory. Each loader routes every stack of the death-loot phase here; any other stack is left alone.

    • onDeath

      public static void onDeath(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.world.damagesource.DamageSource source, Consumer<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack> dropSink)
      Attempt the shears-on-kill harvest, routing the resulting eye through each loader's death-loot phase: Forge adds it to the LivingDropsEvent collection, Fabric appends it from a dropCustomDeathLoot mixin.

    • selfRemoveWithShears

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult selfRemoveWithShears(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand)
      Sneak + right-click air with shears to shear your own eyes off â€” the self-serve counterpart to another player having applied a Slimy Eye to you. One Googly Eye drops carrying your effective appearance and the shears lose one durability. Optometrist shears do it cleanly; plain shears additionally deal one melee hit's worth of ModContent.SELF_SHEAR damage, which has no attacker so PvP and team rules don't cancel it. Returns InteractionResult.PASS when it doesn't apply (not sneaking, not shears, no eyes, googlyEyesEnabled off) so the vanilla item use proceeds.
